svg.title: Negative feedback path — two wires per channel
svg.desc: One channel of the ST-70 has TWO feedback wires returning to the 6GH8A pentode cathode: the main loop sampled at the OPT 16Ω secondary tap (sets closed-loop gain), and a high-frequency compensation path sampled at the OPT UL screen tap (keeps the loop stable). Both terminate at the same summing node.
svg.text: Negative feedback — two wires per channel, one summing node
Main loop (red, solid) from the 16Ω tap sets closed-loop gain. HF compensation (orange, dashed) from the UL tap keeps the loop stable at high frequencies.

g.data-tooltip: INPUT — RCA, switch, grid leak. Audio enters here from the source.

SUMMING JUNCTION — the 6GH8A PENTODE CATHODE.
The audio AC and both feedback signals all meet at this single node. Because the feedback signals are 180° out of phase with the input, they SUBTRACT from it — the pentode sees:
effective_input = audio − k_main·output_16Ω − k_HF·output_UL
The amp's open-loop gain amplifies whatever this difference is, so any deviation from a clean copy of audio gets corrected on the next cycle. That's the feedback mechanism.

6GH8A PENTODE — input voltage amplifier.
Gain ~50×. Its CATHODE (the summing node) is where all the feedback wires arrive. The cathode bias resistor + bypass cap, plus R_fb (main loop) and the 390 pF HF compensation cap, all sit at this node.
6GH8A TRIODE — cathodyne phase splitter. Produces two outputs 180° apart for push-pull.
EL34 PUSH-PULL PAIR — output power stage. Two tubes driving the two halves of the A-470 primary.

A-470 PRIMARY — center-tapped, with UL screen taps (GREEN, GRN/WHT) on each half.
The UL taps are at ~43% of the way from CT to each plate. They carry the audio signal at a high voltage AND with LESS phase shift than the secondary (because they're 'before' the secondary's leakage inductance). That makes them good for HF compensation feedback.

A-470 SECONDARY — speaker-impedance windings. Taps for 4 Ω, 8 Ω, 16 Ω.
The 16Ω tap carries the highest voltage of the secondary taps (best signal-to-noise for the feedback sample), so it's the conventional choice for the main feedback loop.
SPEAKER — the load. The feedback loop wraps around the entire amp INCLUDING the OPT, so the amp 'sees' and corrects for OPT non-linearities too.

svg.text: Two feedback wires return here, both terminating at the pentode cathode

g.data-tooltip:
MAIN FEEDBACK LOOP — from OPT 16Ω secondary tap to pentode cathode.
This is the dominant feedback path that sets the amp's closed-loop gain. About 20 dB of feedback total in the ST-70 (loop gain ~10×). Reduces: • Distortion by ~10× • Output impedance by ~10× (better damping factor) • Bandwidth ripple by ~10×
Trades raw gain for accuracy. The amp doesn't NEED its full open-loop gain — the input source delivers plenty.

HF COMPENSATION LOOP — from OPT primary UL screen tap to pentode cathode through a 390 pF capacitor.
WHY: the OPT itself adds phase shift at high frequencies. Past some frequency, the main loop's phase shift accumulates to where the feedback turns POSITIVE — at which point the amp oscillates.
WHAT THIS FIXES: the UL tap is 'before' the OPT secondary's leakage inductance, so it has less phase shift. Routing a small capacitor (390 pF) from here to the cathode adds a corrective phase ABOVE the audio band, restoring stability margins.
The 390 pF cap blocks low frequencies — at audio frequencies this path contributes negligibly. Only kicks in above a few kHz where it's needed.

WHY TWO SAMPLE POINTS (not one):
Main loop = 16Ω (secondary): represents the actual speaker output. Right place to sample for what the speaker hears.
HF comp = UL (primary): has the audio signal before the OPT's HF phase rotation. Right place to sample for stability.
Together they shape the closed-loop response to be flat AND stable across the audio band.
g.text: The two paths serve different jobs
sets closed-loop gain & reduces distortion across the audio band.
cancels OPT-induced HF phase shift to keep the loop stable.

g.data-tooltip:
The two CHANNELS each have their own pair of feedback wires. Four feedback wires total in the amp.
Right channel: 16Ω → eyelet 13 (step 62) + UL (V6 pin 4) → eyelet 14 (step 48) Left channel: 16Ω → eyelet 12 (step 60) + UL (V3 pin 4) → eyelet 11 (step 58)
g.text: Each channel has its own pair (four feedback wires total)
